description: This Crossrail Learning Legacy technical paper by J. A. Skipper, H. E. Scholes, U. Lawrence, M. Packer and C. Menkiti sets out the geological model of the Lambeth Group that Crossrail Ltd built for the Elizabeth line tunnels under central London, as a record for future projects. Coverage: about 10 km of the tunnel route lies within Lambeth Group sediments; the model draws on 1,043 new ground investigation boreholes drilled since 2000, 653 boreholes from third parties or historical sources, and more than 10,700 tests on these sediments alone. Format and access: a technical paper on the free Learning Legacy site, dated 7 September 2015. Licence and cost: free to read; the site is copyright Crossrail Ltd under its terms and conditions. Caveats: the paper describes the model and its data, not releasing the borehole logs themselves. The stratigraphy, variability and test results inform ground conditions for tunnel hazard exposure and settlement assessments and for capacity planning of new underground rail lines in London. It relates to the BGS geotechnical site investigation records and the JRC Eurocodes portal in the catalogue.
